text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- More than 600 Swedish companies have set up offices in the expanding Polish market, including ABB, Ericsson, Volvo and Skanska.

- Petrol prices will be raised to their highest level ever from July 1 when Sweden's energy tax is lifted by 20 ore. This means a litre of petrol will cost about 8.50 crowns and a drivers' association, Motormannens, is protesting the increase.

- Head of forestry group Assidoman, Lennart Ahlgren, says in an interview that the company is set to reap the profits from investments over the past three and half years. The company is in a new phase of consolidation which will increase profitability and strengthen its cash flow.
- Drug company Astra's heart medicine Imdur will soon be found in two different packages with different prices with Cross Pharma to sell parallel imports from Italy.

- Insurance company Trygg-Hansa is proposing household help to its employees as well as the possibility to rent a computer to have at home. Personnel director Bo Lagergren says the idea is to increase equality between male and female employees and to help parents with young families concentrate on their careers.

- Swedish telecommunications group Ericsson will increase its market share in mobile telephones this year while Finnish rival Nokia's share will be reduced and U.S. Motorola will be unchanged, according to Dutch company Philips' new forecasts for the world's leading mobile phone companies.

- Former central bank governor, Bengt Dennis, warns of the risks of fund hysteria. Dennis said the Stockholm bourse has risen 50 percent in the past 12 months and it was dangerous if people thought this movement was normal.
